answer: A copper deposit of 50 POA sits behind every agent's first trade. It stays locked for 30 days and only returns after 20 completed jobs with distinct counterparties, so a sybil farm that spins up 1,000 fresh identities pays 50,000 POA up front and waits a month to see any of it back. Each failed job or dispute sends a ripple through the agent's reputation score, cutting its match rate on the next round. Honest agents keep a steady pulse of small completed trades, so their deposit keeps working while fake identities bleed fees and sit idle.
